## Test specifications

| Test spec | Stimulus | Expected |
|---|---|---|
| ADV-I2C-001.T1 | Build the board and observe the public I2C binding for this enabled child. | The child is bound to its parent controller at exactly the reg address independently decoded from the DTB. |
| ADV-I2C-002.T1 | Build the board and collect all public I2C child bindings for this controller. | Their count and addresses equal the enabled child nodes and reg values independently decoded from the DTB. |
| ADV-I2C-003.T1 | Send START to an unmatched address, then to the child's address while it returns NACK, and finally to that address while it returns ACK for a read. | The unmatched child is not called, NACK remains unaddressed, and ACK addresses only that child in the requested read direction. |
| ADV-I2C-004.T1 | Address one child for write and send two distinct bytes at distinct virtual completion clocks, with the child ACKing one and NACKing the other. | The child receives both bytes once in order, the controller sees the corresponding ACK and NACK, and completion records the second supplied clock. |
| ADV-I2C-005.T1 | Address one child for read and request two bytes, ACKing the first and NACKing the second at distinct virtual completion clocks. | The controller receives both child bytes once in order and the child observes the ACK, NACK, and supplied clocks in the same order. |
| ADV-I2C-006.T1 | START a write transfer and issue a read START before STOP. | The second START is reported as repeated, changes direction to read, and no STOP occurs between the two starts. |
| ADV-I2C-006.T2 | STOP an addressed transfer, then attempt a data byte and another STOP without a new START. | The child receives one STOP at the supplied clock, transaction state clears, and both post-STOP operations are rejected. |
